rationale: This is a mechanical splice of archive signals "EquityFunded Receivables Inventory Build" and the MIN(equity, NEG cash) conditioner already used in "ProfitableAccrual EquityCashDrawdown," and the MIN-of-ranks construction has repeatedly produced near-zero FMB slopes with only tail-driven alphas in this archive.

Same template as the previous proposal with the debt leg substituted for equity — a combinatorial variant of "AcceleratingDebt WorkingCapitalBuild" and "NonDepAccrual DebtCashDrawdown" rather than a new economic mechanism, and the debt-plus-cash-drawdown conditioner has already delivered strong alpha with a null cross-sectional slope (fmb -0.118), signaling non-monotonicity that this proposal does not address.

A cosmetic swap of the funding leg in the archived "ReceivableTradeCredit FundingGap" for the cash-adjusted version used in gen5/gen6, and it inherits that signal's low coverage (~0.054) without addressing the portfolio-side weakness it claims to fix.

Also a cash-adjusted refinement of an existing pair ("OtherAccrual ExternalFunding Drain," fmb -3.70 but ls_talpha -1.19), but it is internally consistent, targets the specific diagnosed gap between cross-sectional and portfolio evidence, and uses the least-explored txach/aoloch accrual channel — though it is close to the enumeration boundary.

Algebraically identical to the archived "ExternalFunding CashDrain AccrualStrain" — (sstk−prstkc) − Δche − (dltr−dltis) equals (sstk+dltis−prstkc−dltr) − Δche, and both legs are RANK'd the same way, so this is an exact rediscovery of an already-evaluated signal.

The dlc-share/maturity channel has already failed three times in this archive ("Rollover Accrual Fragility," "CurrentDebt Accrual Burden," "AccrualInstability MaturityWall"), and adding the now-standard MIN cash-drawdown gate is a cosmetic conditioner on a repeatedly rejected mechanism.
